reden: Not detected. The report flags reentrancy on the buy path in _handleTrade (refund before state update; no nonReentrant on the single-trade path), which enables bypassing the 10‑minute share lock and stealing CuratorRewardsDistributor funds. However, it does not describe the specific createCred reentrancy scenario where, during the refund callback of buyShareCred invoked inside createCred, an attacker reenters createCred to overwrite creds[credIdCounter] (not yet incremented) and switch the bonding curve to arbitrage buy-then-sell at different curves, draining Ether when multiple curves are whitelisted. The report never mentions reentering createCred, credIdCounter ordering, or bonding-curve switching. While both issues share the broad root cause of reentrancy via ETH refund, they are different code paths/attacks and require different concrete fixes (the described issue specifically needs guarding createCred or otherwise preventing cred overwrite before counter increment). Therefore the specific vulnerability in the description is not captured by the report.
